title: Best Tutorial for RPG Maker MZ or Not Another Tutorial Series?

posts.author: DrFreeman
posts.body:
I had recently been seeing a lot of beginner questions on RPG Maker. I have no problem helping out. Most questions can be answered between the
MZ help
, the
MZ API
, and the
old tutorials
. Some are a bit more tricky requiring using multiple functions together. That got me thinking about making an RPG Maker tutorial series on YouTube. But I saw so many that it made me consider, "Why bother?" I had been using RPG Maker for quite a while, but I changed my approach a lot in MV.
Driftwood Gaming
and
SomeRanDev
had quite a few good tutorials on RPG Maker MV that I would recommend. I also remember Andar had a thread for beginners too with RPG Maker MV. I have to ask are there better ones? In your opinion, what is the best RPG Maker MZ tutorial or does another tutorial series need to be made? Or does the existing content need to be organized in a different way?

posts.author: TotalyNate
posts.body: I always liked Level up Design's tutorials, learned a lot of what I know from him. But also I feel like just getting into the engine and experimenting is as good as any tutorial. But excluding that, the built in tutorials for rmmz aren't bad either.

posts.author: ZombieKidzRule
posts.body:
I strongly support people who have the time, energy, knowledge, and experience making more tutorials for a variety of reasons.
I learned a lot from older tutorials series, but some of them have become somewhat out dated. Some things have changed and some were made when MZ was newish so they aren't necessarily what they would be if they were made today.
Some people might tend to skip over tutorials series that are very old because they might think that aren't as relevant. And some tutorials series may have good content but may be challenging for viewers due to the way things are explained, or an accent, or other things.
Even though I have learned a lot, I would more than welcome a new, well-made, comprehensive tutorials series that goes from the very beginnings of learning MZ to the most advanced concepts.
For my own tutorials (which I don't think are terribly well done and aren't terrific, but I do my best), I tried to focus on things that I hadn't seen a tutorials for yet. So, instead of doing an end-to-end series, I have done more niche tutorials that people might want to do, but there wasn't already a tutorial.
And looking back at my earliest tutorials, I would definitely approach the methods, mechanics, and process differently, now that I have more knowledge and experience. But with limited time, I don't foreseen myself redoing any of those.
Right now I am focusing on trying to make a tutorial series on using Java Script in MZ using the Script event command options. I'm learning Java Script and seeing how to apply all the concepts in MZ, which is sometimes different from that way books and course show using a browser.
So again, I very much appreciate when people take the time to try to help others by making tutorials.
Best of luck!
